subject: Post-call: FintechCo integration & observability hooks
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>, Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@fintechco.com>
Cc: security@fintechco.com
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: FintechCo integration & observability hooks

Thanks for the call today — great discussion. High-level recap and next steps below. Please reply with any corrections.

Quick recap:
- Integrations: SDK + server-side agent to call Redwood endpoints (text generation, embeddings, reranker).
- Auth: we recommended ephemeral API keys (short TTL tokens) OR OIDC-backed service accounts for long-lived server-to-server flows.
- Routing/modeling: route by customer_id header -> model_alias (e.g., rwd-4k-v1) with fallback to cheaper variant for non-critical queries.
- Structured output/tool-calling: use the SDK's function-calling helpers and include schema validation on the client side.
- Observability: propagate trace ids; emit token-level latency breakdown headers for debugging.

Concrete next steps (for FintechCo):
1) Confirm preferred auth method (ephemeral API keys vs OIDC). If OIDC, share issuer and jwks endpoint.
2) Share a sample request flow (frontend -> backend -> Redwood) so we can confirm trace-id propagation points.
3) Decide on embedding storage (existing vector DB or Redwood-managed embeddings API + webhook).
4) Schedule a short follow-up with our infra engineer to review rate limits and IP allowlist.

Integration notes (SDK/auth/routing):
- SDK boot: set API key in env or use SDK.setAuthBearer(token). Example snippet attached (sample_env.sh).
- Auth patterns: for user-specific inference, mint ephemeral keys from your session service and pass to client. For backend-only flows, use server-side service account keys.
- Routing: include X-Redwood-Route: customer_id=fintechco;model_alias=rwd-4k-v1 in request headers to enable deterministic routing.

Observability hooks (initial recommendations):
- Trace ID: propagate X-Redwood-Trace-Id (UUID v4). If absent, Redwood runtime will generate and return it in response headers.
- Logging fields: include request_id (your UUID), user_id (if available), model_version, route. Redwood logs will include these fields to join traces.
- Latency breakdown: responses include X-Redwood-Latency-Breakdown: "total_ms=120;tokenize_ms=8;model_ms=95;encode_ms=17" for per-request debugging.
- Dashboards: per-route latency + cost panels; example dashboard link attached.

Attachments: fintechco-integration-checklist.pdf, sample_env.sh, observability_headers.md

Happy to iterate — propose we aim to confirm auth method and schedule the infra deep-dive by end of next week.

—Marissa

On Thu, Jun 11, 2026 at 09:03 AM Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com> wrote:
> Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A couple quick follow-ups from our engineering team: 
> 
> 1) Embeddings: we plan to store vectors in our existing Pinecone cluster. Any recommended encoder/embedding-size? Also, how do you recommend we handle reranking latency if we call an embeddings reranker in the hot path?
> 
> 2) Trace propagation: frontend will send a trace UUID (our own request_id). Do you recommend we set X-Redwood-Trace-Id to the same value or send both (request_id + X-Redwood-Trace-Id)? What should we expect to see in the final logs/headers?
> 
> 3) SDK snippet: can you share the exact header name for auth and the minimal JS example to set it (server-side)?

Great questions — answers below. Attaching observability_headers.md with header examples and the integration checklist.

1) Embeddings & reranker guidance:
- Encoder: use our rwd-embed-1024 encoder for best semantic recall (512 or 1024 dims depending on your budget). 1024 recommended for financial QA/semantic search.
- Storage: match the vector dim in Pinecone; store metadata with trace_id and model_version to join records.
- Reranker latency patterns: keep the reranker model off the critical UI path where possible; run a fast embedding-based candidate retrieval (0-50ms) then lightweight rerank on top. If reranker needs to be immediate, provision a dedicated low-latency model alias and enable caching for repeated queries.

2) Trace propagation recommendations:
- We recommend using your request_id as the canonical trace id. Set X-Redwood-Trace-Id: <your-request-id> on the request to Redwood. Redwood will echo the same ID in response headers and logs so you can correlate easily. You may also include X-Request-Id: <your-request-id> for your internal logs — Redwood will ingest X-Redwood-Trace-Id for its traces.
- Example response header: X-Redwood-Latency-Breakdown: total_ms=128;tokenize_ms=9;model_ms=102;encode_ms=17

3) Minimal JS SDK auth snippet (server-side):
- Header: Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY_OR_EPHEMERAL_TOKEN>
- Example:
  const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference');
  const client = new Redwood.Client({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
  // or explicitly set bearer at runtime
  client.setAuthBearer(ephemeralToken);

Observability implementation notes:
- Propagate X-Redwood-Trace-Id from your frontend through your backend. If absent, Redwood will generate a UUID and return it in the response.
- Include model_version and route in your logs. We recommend adding these fields to any structured logs so you can join service logs and Redwood logs in your SIEM.

Links and attachments: observability_headers.md (header examples), fintechco-integration-checklist.pdf (next steps), sample_env.sh (SDK snippet).

Would you like our infra engineer to join the next call next Tue/Wed? I'm free Tue afternoon PT.

—Marissa
